label: def:index
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:index}
The differentiation index $\nu$ of~\eqref{eq:dyn} is the minimum number of differentiations of the algebraic constraint required to obtain an explicit ODE via algebraic manipulations.
head: environment
name: Differentiation index

label: assumption:regularity
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{assumption:regularity}
For all $x\in\mathcal{C}\cap\mathcal{M}$, the algebraic Jacobian $J_a(x)\in\mathbb{R}^{n_m\times n_a}$ is square and nonsingular, i.e., $n_m=n_a$ and $\det(J_a(x))\neq 0$.
head: environment
name: Regularity

label: def:positive_invariance
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:positive_invariance}
A set $\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_x}$ is \emph{positively invariant} under~\eqref{eq:dyn} and policy $\mu$ if $x(0)\in\mathcal{C}$ and $u(t)=\mu(x(t))$ for all $t\geq 0$ implies $x(t)\in\mathcal{C}$ for all $t\geq 0$.

name: Safety

label: theorem:CBF_safety
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: \hspace{-0.01cm

label: problem:dae_cbf
title: Problem
body_md:
\label{problem:dae_cbf}
Given a semi-explicit DAE~\eqref{eq:dyn} satisfying Assumption~\ref{assumption:regularity}, a safe set $\mathcal{C}$, and a candidate barrier function $b(x)$: \textit{(i)}~design a control policy $\mu:\mathbb{R}^{n_x}\to\mathbb{R}^{n_u}$ such that $\mathcal{D}\cap\mathcal{M}$ is positively invariant for all $x(0)\in\mathcal{D}\cap\mathcal{M}$; and \textit{(ii)}~verify that the resulting safety filter is both correct ($\mathcal{D}\cap\mathcal{M}\subseteq\mathcal{C}\cap\mathcal{M}$) and feasible (a compatible, safe input exists at every state).

label: remark:reduction_to_ode
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{remark:reduction_to_ode}
For regular index-1 DAEs with $n_m=n_a$, $J_a(x)$ is square and invertible on $\mathcal{C}\cap\mathcal{M}$, so $J_a(x)^\dagger=J_a(x)^{-1}$ and $P(x)=I_{n_m}-J_a J_a^{-1}=0$. The compatibility condition then drops from the DAE-aware CBF-QP. However, the CBF inequality itself \emph{still} uses the projected fields $(\hat{f},\hat{g})$ from~\eqref{eq:projected_fields}, which differ from the original $(f,g)$. For~\eqref{eq:projected_fields}, the lower blocks $-J_a^{-1}J_d f_d$ and $-J_a^{-1}J_d g_d$ encode how the algebraic states respond to the differential dynamics. A naive CBF evaluated along $(f,g)$ ignores this coupling and can drive trajectories off $\mathcal{M}$. The consistency with algebraic constraints, thus, is enforced by both the projected fields~\eqref{eq:projected_fields} and the compatibility constraint~\eqref{eq:compatibility}.
head: environment

label: thm:positive_invariance
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Safety of semi-explicit DAEs

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\phi$ does not depend on the control input, differentiating $\phi(x(t))=0$ and substituting $\dot{x}_d=f_d(x)+g_d(x)u$ yields the compatibility condition~\eqref{eq:compatibility}. Thus, condition~\eqref{eq:compat_cond} is equivalent to~\eqref{eq:compatibility}. Now, for $
u=1$, $J_a(x)$ is nonsingular on $\mathcal{C}\cap\mathcal{M}$ (Assumption~ef{assumption:regularity}), thus $\dot{x}_a$ is uniquely determined by~\eqref{eq:xa_dot} and the projected fields~\eqref{eq:projected_fields} are well-defined with $
abla\phi(x)\hat{f}(x)=0$ and $
abla\phi(x)\hat{g}(x)=0$. Hence any trajectory of $\dot{x}=\hat{f}(x)+\hat{g}(x)u$ starting on $\mathcal{M}$ remains on $\mathcal{M}$, and differentiating $b$ along the projected dynamics gives $\dot{b}(x(t))=\mathcal{L}_{\hat{f}}b(x)+\mathcal{L}_{\hat{g}}b(x)u$.
Thus,~\eqref{eq:cbf_cond} yields $\dot{b}\geq -\alpha(b)$, where for $\alpha\in\mathcal{K}_\infty$ with $\alpha(0)=0$ and $b(x(0))\geq 0$, the comparison lemma~\cite[Lemma~3.4]{khalil2002nonlinear} gives $b(x(t))\geq 0$ for all $t\geq 0$. Based on that, any trajectory starting in $\mathcal{D}\cap\mathcal{M}$ remains in $\mathcal{D}\cap\mathcal{M}$.

label: cor:autonomous_index1
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Autonomous DAEs

title: Proof
body_md: Set $u\equiv 0$ in~\eqref{eq:invariance_conditions}. Condition~\eqref{eq:compat_cond} reduces to~\eqref{eq:autonomous_compat}, and condition~\eqref{eq:cbf_cond} reduces to~\eqref{eq:autonomous_cbf}. The proof then follows directly from Theorem~\ref{thm:positive_invariance}.

label: def:relative_degree
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:relative_degree}
The \emph{relative degree} of a smooth function $b(x)$ with respect to a control affine system $\dot{x}=f(x)+g(x)u$ is $d\geq 1$ if $d$ is the smallest integer such that \textit{(i)} $\mathcal{L}_g\mathcal{L}_f^k b(x)=0$ for all $k<d-1$; and \textit{(ii)} $\mathcal{L}_g\mathcal{L}_f^{d-1}b(x)\neq 0$.
head: environment
name: Relative degree

label: lem:index_rel_degree
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:index_rel_degree}
Consider the DAE system~\eqref{eq:dyn} satisfying Assumption~ef{assumption:regularity}. Let $d'$ denote the smallest integer such that $J_d(x)\mathcal{L}_{g_d}\mathcal{L}_{f_d}^{d'-1}x_d(x)
eq 0$. Then, the relative degree, $d$, of the algebraic constraint $\phi(x)$ with respect to system~\eqref{eq:dyn} satisfies $d=
u+d'-1$. For index-1 systems ($
u=1$), we have $d=d'$.
head: environment
name: Index and relative degree

title: Proof
body_md:
For a single differentiation of $\phi(x(t))=0$, the compatibility condition~\eqref{eq:compatibility} yields $J_d(x)\dot{x}_d+J_a(x)\dot{x}_a=0$. Since $
u=1$, $J_a(x)$ is invertible and $\dot{x}_a$ is determined by $\dot{x}_d$. The control $u$ appears in the $
u$-th derivative of $\phi$ through $J_d(x)$; for $u$ to have a nonzero coefficient, $d'$ additional derivatives of $x_d$ through $J_d(x)$ are required (Definition~ef{def:relative_degree}). Hence $d=
u+d'-1$, and for $
u=1$, $d=d'$.

label: cor:hocbf
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: DAE-aware HOCBF for semi-explicit systems

title: Proof
body_md: Condition~\eqref{eq:hocbf_compat} ensures $x(t)\in\mathcal{M}$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:positive_invariance}. On $\mathcal{M}$, the dynamics can be written as $\dot{x}=\hat{f}(x)+\hat{g}(x)u$, and $b(x)$ has relative degree $d$ with respect to this system (Definition~\ref{def:relative_degree}). Condition~\eqref{eq:hocbf_cbf} is the HOCBF condition~\cite{xiao2021high} applied to the projected dynamics, giving $b(x(t))\geq 0$ via iterated comparison arguments.
head: environment

label: def:valid_dae_cbf
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:valid_dae_cbf}
A smooth function $b:\mathbb{R}^{n_x}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a \emph{valid DAE-aware CBF} for the safe set $\mathcal{C}$ under DAE~\eqref{eq:dyn} if \textit{(i)}~$\mathcal{D}\cap\mathcal{M}\subseteq\mathcal{C}\cap\mathcal{M}$ (correctness); and \textit{(ii)}~for every $x\in\mathcal{D}\cap\mathcal{M}$, there exists $u\in\mathcal{U}$ satisfying~\eqref{eq:invariance_conditions} (feasibility).
head: environment
name: Valid DAE-aware CBF

label: problem:verification
title: Problem
body_md:
\label{problem:verification}
Given a candidate DAE-aware CBF $b:\mathbb{R}^{n_x}\to\mathbb{R}$, verify \textit{(i)}~\emph{correctness}, i.e., $\mathcal{D}\cap\mathcal{M}\subseteq\mathcal{C}\cap\mathcal{M}$; and \textit{(ii)}~\emph{feasibility}, i.e., for every $x\in\mathcal{D}\cap\mathcal{M}$, there exists $u\in\mathcal{U}$ such that~\eqref{eq:invariance_conditions} holds.

label: thm:psatz
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:psatz}
The set $\{x\in\mathbb{R}^{n_x}:\Phi_i(x)\geq 0,\;\chi_j(x)\neq 0,\;\Gamma_\ell(x)=0\}$ is empty iff there exist $\Phi\in\Sigma$, $\chi\in\mathcal{N}$, and $\Gamma\in\mathbb{I}$ such that $\Phi+\chi^2+\Gamma=0$.
head: environment

label: lem:correctness
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Correctness via Psatz

title: Proof
body_md: Identity~\eqref{eq:correctness_identity} certifies $\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{viol}}=\emptyset$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:psatz} applied to the cone generated by $b$ and $-h-s^2$, the monoid generated by $s$, and the ideal generated by $\phi_\ell$. Emptiness of $\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{viol}}$ implies that no $x\in\mathcal{D}\cap\mathcal{M}$ satisfies $h(x)<0$, i.e., $\mathcal{D}\cap\mathcal{M}\subseteq\mathcal{C}\cap\mathcal{M}$.
head: environment

label: lem:farkas
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:farkas}
The system $Au\leq r$ has a solution iff there is no $\lambda\geq 0$ with $\lambda^\top A=0^\top$ and $\lambda^\top r<0$.
head: environment
name: Farkas' Lemma

label: thm:verification
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: DAE-aware CBF verification

title: Proof
body_md: By Lemma~\ref{lem:farkas}, $A_{\mathrm{int}}(x)u\leq r_{\mathrm{int}}(x)$ is feasible if and only if condition~2 holds, and $A_{\mathrm{bnd}}(x)u\leq r_{\mathrm{bnd}}(x)$ is feasible if and only if condition~3 holds. Together, these guarantee the existence of admissible inputs satisfying compatibility and input bounds at interior points, and additionally the tangency condition at boundary points. Positive invariance of $\mathcal{D}\cap\mathcal{M}$ then follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:positive_invariance}.
head: environment

label: prop:sos_certificates
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Polynomial DAE-aware certificates

title: Proof
body_md: The proof follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:farkas}. The interior and boundary dual systems are infeasible iff their semialgebraic representations are empty. Theorem~\ref{thm:psatz} then certifies such emptiness through the stated cone, monoid, and ideal identities. Given that all functions are polynomial, this is reduced to an SOS feasibility program.
head: environment
